claims.text: A July 2016 Ops Manager 1.8-to-2.0 upgrade account records the daemon becoming part of the Ops Manager RPM and recommends performing a backup after upgrading to verify daemon operation. This is historical upgrade evidence. (low confidence)

The Ops Manager package installs the Backup Daemon component, but administrators must activate it to use it; the host service also has separate start, stop, restart, and status commands. (medium confidence)
Administrators manage the daemon process through /etc/init.d/mongodb-mms-backup-daemon with start, stop, restart, and status commands. (low confidence)

The administration API creates an initial daemon configuration with PUT /daemon/configs/{MACHINE}, requiring the daemon process to be running first. Updating an existing configuration uses PUT /daemon/configs/{MACHINE}/{HEAD-ROOT-DIRECTORY}. (high confidence)
Assignment labels restrict which backup jobs a daemon can process. Without labels, the daemon can process only jobs from projects that do not filter their jobs with labels. (high confidence)
machine.headRootDirectory must end with a slash; omitting it causes a Java exception. Update requests must URL-encode directory slashes in the endpoint path. (high confidence)

A March 2023 operator report for Ops Manager 6.0.11 records BackupDaemonPreFlightCheck repeatedly waiting for a system upgrade before starting. The forum response recommends support investigation and does not establish a root cause or a verified repair. (low confidence)
The Ops Manager Backup Daemon performs backup maintenance, including groom jobs and queryable restores; it also creates incremental snapshots when using filesystem stores. (high confidence)

Administrators can dedicate a daemon to queryable restore work by disabling its other job types. The configuration API separately exposes backupJobsEnabled, garbageCollectionEnabled, and restoreQueryableJobsEnabled, with numWorkers controlling worker processes. (medium confidence)

For initial daemon configuration, the documented API uses PUT /api/public/v1.0/admin/backup/daemon/configs/{MACHINE}; the daemon process must already be running. An already configured daemon should use the update endpoint. (low confidence)

Ops Manager can run Backup Daemon maintenance on any configured application instance. The daemon runs grooming, incremental filesystem snapshot work, and queryable restores; client applications cannot communicate directly with it, and its state and job queues come from the Application Database. (low confidence)
Client applications cannot communicate directly with the Backup Daemon; its state and job queues come from the Ops Manager Application Database. (low confidence)

Stack Harbor, which says it operates client Ops Manager deployments, recommends sizing backup-daemon storage and IOPS for the total managed dataset and including the daemon in ongoing monitoring and upgrades. This is practitioner guidance rather than a MongoDB sizing formula. (low confidence)

Multiple Backup Daemons can increase concurrent job capacity and provide manual failover. Deploying multiple application hosts behind a load balancer does not remove the requirement to run at least one Backup Daemon. (high confidence)

Daemon configuration separates assignmentEnabled, backupJobsEnabled, garbageCollectionEnabled, restoreQueryableJobsEnabled, and resourceUsageEnabled. numWorkers controls worker processes for backup, restore, or grooming tasks. (high confidence)

The MongoDB Enterprise Kubernetes Operator 1.14.0 release notes document a fix for a custom CA not being mounted into the Backup Daemon pod, which had prevented backups in hybrid-mode deployments using a custom CA. (low confidence)

In its July 28, 2026 description of NDB 2.11 shard scale-out, Nutanix says NDB refreshes Ops Manager backup-daemon job references for the expanded topology before resuming protection and triggering a fresh baseline snapshot. This describes NDB integration behavior. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-07-28)

NetBackup's MongoDB Ops Manager Administrator's Guide 11.1 requires clusters protected through its integration to be marked Third Party Managed in Ops Manager; its architecture retains Ops Manager in the protection workflow. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23)

Multiple Backup Daemons increase concurrent job capacity and provide manual failover. After a daemon host fails, a Global Owner or global backup administrator can move its jobs to another daemon. (high confidence)
